summary: Use see-through appearance selectively to reveal depth, thickness or nested structure while keeping an opaque reference where needed.
objective: The outer contour and intended interior remain distinguishable, and transparent parts do not disappear against the background.
intent_signals: Create a glass-like or translucent appearance
Reveal nested forms while preserving the outer contour
example_prompts: Create a translucent nested-solid sculpture with a readable outer contour and optional opaque comparison.

principles: Use see-through appearance selectively to reveal depth, thickness or nested structure while keeping an opaque reference where needed.
implementation: Model the boundaries and thickness that the chosen visual explanation needs; simplify overlapping layers that offer no useful information.
Try broad reflection shapes and contrasting backgrounds; treat colors and apparent transparency as authored presentation choices until independently specified.
Use an orbit that reveals both silhouette and interior; animate layer separation or a single object rather than all overlapping surfaces at once.

Set scene.environment from PMREMGenerator.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment()) or an HDRI before enabling transmission; MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission 0.95, thickness 0.6-2.5, ior 1.5 and roughness 0.05 renders as an opaque dark shape without an environment.

Place a two-value backdrop (#16202b against #dfe7ef) behind the subject and keep one opaque interior part at or below 0.35 roughness, then confirm by screenshot that the outer contour survives against both halves.
observable_checks: The outer contour and intended interior remain distinguishable, and transparent parts do not disappear against the background.

defaults.rationale: Glass has no colour of its own on screen - it borrows the environment - so the numbers require an environment map, keep the tint below 25% saturation and let thickness and attenuation distance rather than albedo carry the hue. Broad RectAreaLight sources at a 3:1 ratio are specified because a transparent object is read through the shape of the source reflected in it, and the split light/dark backdrop guarantees every silhouette edge crosses a value change instead of vanishing.

values.value_structure: 30/40/30 dark/mid/light with a deliberate light-to-dark backdrop split, so every glass edge crosses a value boundary and cannot disappear
values.saturation_rule: glass tint <= 25% HSL because colour should come from thickness rather than albedo; the opaque interior reference may reach 55%

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 3:1; glass is read through the shape of the reflected source, so the source proportions matter more than its intensity

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission 0.95, thickness 0.6-2.5 (metres of glass path), ior 1.45-1.52, roughness 0.02-0.1 polished or 0.25-0.35 frosted, attenuationColor #7fb6c9 at attenuationDistance 0.8; scene.environment via PMREM is mandatory or transmission renders black

post.dof: front glass surface in focus at f/5.6 for stills; off during orbit

values.signature_technique: a split backdrop, dark on one side and light on the other, so each glass edge crosses a value boundary and the silhouette is defined by refraction contrast rather than by an outline
never: every layer transparent at once with no opaque interior reference
glass on a flat black background
thickness left at 0, which renders a coloured film rather than a solid

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0; re-tune every intensity, fog density and bloom threshold if you change the tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with monochrome, technical illustration or miniature accents; appearance guidance does not specify optical constants or a renderer algorithm.
